transcript_text:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2025-10-02 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Host: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood)
- Attendees: Sofia (AE), Marcus (SE), Talia (Partner GTM) from Redwood; Rajiv (VP Eng), Elena (Head of AI), Tom (Procurement) from Meridian

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood + Meridian alignment on joint go-to-market (winplay), technical risk gates for a pilot, and procurement timeline. Main concerns: data residency, SOC2/KMS, latency vs cost for clinical inference, and co-sell economics. Agreed next steps: bench tests, draft winplay, partner intro, and procurement timeline.

Topics:
- Joint winplay positioning for payer/provider customers
- Technical gating: VPC/private control plane, KMS, on-prem options
- Pilot scoping: 2-3 clinical workflows, latency SLOs, success metrics
- Commercial: co-sell credit, deal registration, pricing guardrails

Action items: (captured above, auto-list; see explicit action items for owners)

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Alvarez: hey everyone uh thanks for joining on time, we've got about 45 minutes, I wanted to kickoff with quick context from Talia on the partner motion then go into the technical risk gates and attach the commercial ask, is that cool?
[00:12] Talia Brooks: yeah this is Talia from the partner side, thanks for making time Rajiv, Elena - our ask is simple, Meridian is a top target vertical for us, we think joint references in healthcare will unlock several enterprise deals, so the winplay is to position you as technical reference + proof of concept customer, and Redwood provides co-sell credits, joint logos, and joint exec briefing.
[00:35] Rajiv Patel: thanks, yes we've seen your exec brief, happy to explore but we have strict constraints on patient data residency and encryption, and our security team will not accept any ambiguity on key management.
[00:48] Marcus Chen: absolutely, we run private deployments and dedicated pools, we also support a VPC private control plane option - sorry, it sometimes shows up in notes as Redwood Private, but technically there's a private control plane with optional on-prem agent. For KMS, we integrate with customer KMS and HSMs, we can also do envelope encryption.
[01:12] Elena Morris: quick question, when you say "private control plane" is that fully air-gapped or just VPC peering. We are regulated so air-gap for PHI workflows might be necessary.
[01:24] Marcus Chen: good question, short answer: both. We have a VPC-hosted private control plane for most customers, and an on-prem package that can be deployed behind firewall for air-gap—there are caveats around telemetry and updates, but it is a supported path. It was in our docs as Redwood Private but sometimes transcribed in call notes as "Redwood Privet" or "Redwood Privatee" so apologies for inconsistent naming in earlier docs.
[01:47] Rajiv Patel: ok that's clarifying. Another gating item is SOC2 and ISO, do you have a current report?
[01:54] Sofia Alvarez: yes we have SOC2 Type II and we're in the process of ISO 27001 certification, I will share the SOC2 report via the secure link, and Marcus will include the controls mapping.
[02:08] Tom Li: procurement question up front - what's the minimum contract value for co-sell credits? Also do you support net-60 invoicing?
[02:16] Talia Brooks: so for co-sell credit we typically have a minimum of a $75k ARR commit for joint logos to qualify for the standard co-sell package, but we can be flexible for strategic wins - will take that offline. Net-60 is something we can discuss with finance; it's not default but we've accommodated customers with approvals.
[02:41] (crosstalk)
[02:44] Elena Morris: performance note — our workflows are real-time-ish clinical assistant calls, we need tail latency under 250ms for short prompts, avg throughput of 120 concurrent sessions during peak. Can you meet that on hosted?
[02:58] Marcus Chen: hypothetically yes but depends on model variant, quantization profile, and batching. For hosted API we optimize for throughput with continuous batching which can add variability to tail latency. For strict 250ms SLOs we typically recommend Dedicated with pinned GPUs and a latency-first config; also prefix-KV caching helps if you have repeated context. We should run a bench with your sample prompts to know for sure.
[03:24] Rajiv Patel: what's the delta on cost for Dedicated vs Hosted? A ballpark per 1M tokens?
[03:30] Marcus Chen: rough rule: hosted is simple per-token; dedicated is capacity-based so unit cost can be lower at scale if you fully utilize. For a clinical assistant scenario with many short sessions, dedicated often pays off after you hit steady concurrency — but we need to model your concurrency curve. Marcus: I'll run a 10k token workload bench and give a per-token estimate vs hosted.
[03:52] Sofia Alvarez: one more commercial nuance: for co-sell we'll want joint marketing and a short customer reference period; Talia will manage that. We also need to align on procurement timing so Redwood's sales ops can scope discounts in the quote.
[04:06] Tom Li: procurement timeline — we expect a vendor review first week of Nov, legal review takes 2-3 weeks after vendor review, and budget signoff planned by mid-Nov. So POC needs to start by mid-Oct if we want production by Q1.
[04:23] Elena Morris: about PII/PHI — we will only share de-identified sample prompts for benching until legal signs off, but we can give representative latency-critical prompts.
[04:34] Marcus Chen: that's fine; we can mock PHI with structured placeholders and still benchmark latency and KV-cache behavior. Also, for privacy we can run the bench in your VPC with a device in your region to match routing.
[04:50] Rajiv Patel: on the product side, we need to confirm model version pinning and rollout controls — we cannot have silent model upgrades that change behavior in production.
[04:58] Marcus Chen: absolutely, Redwood supports model pinning and staged rollouts with canary and automatic fallback policy. We'll add that to the controls doc. A note — sometimes our docs call it "rollouts" or "rollouts and fallback" and the speech-to-text might have spelled it wrong in earlier notes.
[05:12] (short pause)
[05:17] Sofia Alvarez: switching to winplay — Talia do you want to outline the suggested customer-facing narrative and what Redwood will commit for the joint motion?
[05:23] Talia Brooks: yes, recommended winplay: 1) Proof of concept for Meridian's clinical assistant (three workflows), 2) co-branded case study after successful POC, 3) two exec briefings for sales cycles, and 4) 6-8 weeks of discounted pilot pricing. Partner concessions: co-sell credit for first-year ARR, and joint lead routing. We'll circulate a one-pager winplay doc post-call.
[05:45] Rajiv Patel: for the case study, legal will need to review what we can publicize. We may agree to a joint logo but not patient narratives.
[05:53] Talia Brooks: totally understood. We'll scope the case study to operational metrics and anonymized quotes.
[05:59] Elena Morris: technical ask — we'd like a simple SLA: 99.5% uptime for the dedicated cluster and latency SLO penalties if the tail exceeds 250ms more than 1% of requests. Is that something you can commit to in a pilot?
[06:14] Marcus Chen: we can provide a pilot SLA with monitoring and a corrective action plan; financial penalties at pilot stage are unusual but we can do service credits on escalation. If you need hard financial SLAs we should move to a Dedicated reserved contract.
[06:30] Rajiv Patel: ok can we do a 6-week pilot with 2-week ramp, and include a technical checkpoint at week 3 for latency/growth?
[06:37] Sofia Alvarez: yes that's reasonable. We'll propose a pilot scope doc that includes success metrics and check points.
[06:43] Tom Li: procurement — if pilot is paid and credited toward production, procurement needs PO terms, invoice schedule, and SSO/SCIM contract addendum.
[06:52] Sofia Alvarez: we can do paid pilot credited toward future commitment; Marcus will include SSO/SCIM integration notes and our security addendum.
[06:59] (short overlap, inaudible)
[07:03] Elena Morris: on the bench, we care about cold-start vs warm-start latencies and also the tokenization behavior for clinical shorthand. Please capture both.
[07:12] Marcus Chen: will do — I'll run cold and warm benchmarks, p95/p99 numbers, and also test with quantized vs FP16 variants. We'll include memory/kv cache utilization metrics too.
[07:22] Rajiv Patel: any concerns about model hallucinations with medical prompts? We'll need guardrails and evals to track regressions.
[07:29] Marcus Chen: Redwood Optimize has a quality monitoring feature; we can instrument prompt sets and regression alerts. For high-risk outputs we recommend retrieval-augmented prompting and reranking layers. We'll show a demo of reranker options in the follow-up session if helpful.
[07:47] Sofia Alvarez: ok let's clarify commercial asks — Meridian wants pilot discounted then potential committed Dedicated capacity. Are we offering partner discounts or margin to Meridian? Talia?
[07:57] Talia Brooks: partner co-sell economics: Meridian will benefit from a reduced pilot fee; if the deal converts to committed Dedicated we typically roll a co-sell credit against first-year ARR. Specific margin for partners depends on the partner contract. I'll share the co-sell schedule.
[08:12] Tom Li: also, will Redwood accept a two-step PO where we issue PO for pilot and then issue a second PO for production? This aligns with our internal procurement.
[08:20] Sofia Alvarez: yes accepted, we generally accept staged POs; Marcus and finance will align with procurement terms.
[08:27] (brief silence as notes recorded)
[08:31] Elena Morris: one more technical nuance — our infra team prefers cert pinning and limited outbound egress for any control-plane components. Can you support that?
[08:39] Marcus Chen: yes, cert pinning is supported and outbound egress can be restricted; the on-prem option removes outbound telemetry unless enabled. We'll detail network egress rules in the controls mapping doc.
[08:52] Rajiv Patel: any blockers on IP/ownership? We need clarity that Meridian owns any derivatives they create and what logs Redwood retains.
[09:00] Sofia Alvarez: good call — we'll provide an IP appendix that clarifies customer outputs and Redwood logs; our default is customer owns their outputs and we retain anonymized telemetry for product improvement unless otherwise agreed.
[09:14] (someone coughs)
[09:18] Talia Brooks: last thing from partner side — we want to align on who will own the sales pursuit motions. My suggestion is Redwood AE/Sales rep owns Redwood-side GTM, Meridian will provide an internal sponsor, and we'll schedule joint exec briefing 2 weeks after the pilot acceptance.
[09:35] Rajiv Patel: I can be the internal sponsor for Meridian.
[09:38] Sofia Alvarez: perfect, Rajiv. We'll draft a 1-pager winplay and a pilot scope doc and share by Monday. Marcus will run bench, Talia will share co-sell schedule, Elena to share prompt set.
[09:52] Tom Li: procurement will aim to have initial PO for pilot by 2025-10-20 if docs align.
[09:58] Sofia Alvarez: great — any final questions?
[10:02] Elena Morris: just, will you also provide a list of recommended model variants and quantization profiles for clinical safety?
[10:09] Marcus Chen: yes, I'll include recommended model families, quantization tradeoffs, and expected tokenization behavior.
[10:14] Sofia Alvarez: awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and schedule the bench kickoff.
[10:21] (meeting ends)

Post-Call Notes (auto-generated):
- Pilot scope: 6-week paid pilot credited to first-year ARR, 2-week ramp, week-3 tech checkpoint.
- Bench: Marcus to run cold/warm p95/p99 latency tests, quantized vs fp16, KV-cache tests, using anonymized prompts.
- Security: Redwood to share SOC2, controls mapping, and KMS/HSM integration docs.
- Commercial: co-sell credit for first-year ARR, staged PO accepted, procurement aiming for pilot PO by 2025-10-20.
